page: Microsoft Azure D64ps_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by the 64-bit ARMv8 architecture. It is built with 64 dedicated physical Ampere Neoverse-N1 cores operating at a base frequency of 3.0 GHz with one thread per core. The hardware configuration features 208 GB of system RAM, allocating 3.25 GB of memory per core. Cache hierarchy includes 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. This instance type contains no integrated GPUs and includes no local SSD storage, necessitating the attachment of remote Premium Storage volumes for disk operations.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel efficiency across multi-threaded applications. The server achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 112,414.59 and completed Geekbench Clang software compilation workloads with a score of 47,010.0, both placing in the top 25 percent of tested systems. Cached memory bandwidth for small blocks reached 4,385.45 GB/sec, which aligns with strong in-memory key-value processing, evidenced by 80.8 million Redis SET operations per second. Conversely, single-threaded throughput is comparatively moderate, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,113.0 and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 8.85 GB/sec placing in the lower quartile.

The D64ps_v5 offers favorable resource density for multi-threaded systems by providing dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading interference. However, lack of local disk storage requires engineering consideration for external storage throughput, and workloads demanding x86-specific vector extensions such as AVX-512 are unsupported. This server profile is best suited for concurrent compilation pipelines, containerized microservices, distributed in-memory caching systems, and scale-out web application deployments.
description: Microsoft Azure D64ps_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on 64 dedicated Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 cores operating at 3.0 GHz with a single thread per core. It provides 208 GB of system RAM, equating to 3.25 GB per vCPU, alongside a 32 MB L3 cache. The instance features no bundled local storage and lacks GPU acceleration, relying entirely on network-attached remote storage. Performance benchmarks highlight strong multi-core scaling, with upper-quartile results in multi-threaded CPU stress testing, Clang software compilation, and Redis SET throughput exceeding 80 million operations per second. In contrast, single-core computational metrics such as Geekbench single-core and single-threaded compression fall into lower percentiles. Given its high core count and absence of simultaneous multithreading, the D64ps_v5 is suited for parallel scale-out workloads, including continuous integration build farms, container orchestration nodes, and distributed in-memory data tiers.
